issues.description: delimiter parameter conflates literal characters with OpenAPI symbolic style names in one namespace.
issues.detail: The delimiter kwarg accepts both raw characters (',', '|', ' ') and style names ('pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited') through one keyword, mixing two vocabularies. The _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict reflects this by mixing identity entries with aliases. Separate the allowed character set from the alias map, or pick one vocabulary, so the precondition is expressible as one clean predicate.

issues.description: Raising bare ValueError for a bad delimiter conflates programmer error with malformed client input.
issues.detail: get_param_as_list converts ValueError from transforms into HTTPBadRequest. An unsupported delimiter is a developer-contract violation, not bad client input, but raising plain ValueError risks being reported to the client as 400 or swallowed by surrounding handling. Use a distinct exception type (TypeError or a precondition assertion) and validate once at the boundary, not on every hot-path call.

issues.description: Identity entries in _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS are redundant and obscure intent.
issues.detail: Half the dict maps ',' to ',', '|' to '|', ' ' to ' ' purely to make membership-checking work, while only two entries are real aliases. Decompose into an allowlist set of characters plus a small alias map {'pipeDelimited': '|', 'spaceDelimited': ' '}. Two concepts, two values, and the table becomes self-explanatory.

issues.description: Silent no-op when items is already a list contradicts the caller's split request.
issues.detail: When the same parameter appears multiple times, items arrives as a list and the delimiter argument is silently ignored. A caller asking for pipe-splitting may get list members that still contain pipes. The behavior is documented as a Note but the postcondition the caller actually gets is not stated as a contract; either split list members too or raise, but don't silently disagree.

issues.description: Tests miss boundary cases: blank tokens, default path regression, and transform interaction.
issues.detail: The new tests cover happy paths and the unsupported-delimiter rejection but not: empty/blank tokens after split ('a,,b'), keep_blank_qs_values interaction, delimiter combined with transform, default returned when missing, and the delimiter=None default-path regression on a comma-containing value. Pin these so the next maintainer doesn't have to guess and so the spec is proved, not merely demonstrated.

synthesis.summary: The patch is small, well-scoped, and structurally clean — one method, one new kwarg, overloads and news fragment included. The panel's consensus concern is at the specification layer: the delimiter parameter complects literal characters with OpenAPI style names in one keyword, and the _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict reflects that by mixing identity entries with aliases. A second consensus concern is error-channel hygiene — raising bare ValueError for a programmer mistake risks being mistranslated into HTTPBadRequest. Tests demonstrate happy paths but leave boundary behavior (blank tokens, default path, transform interaction) unpinned. Land-worthy after the noted cleanups.
